title: Homemade lemonade
intro: Peel steeped in the syrup brings aroma; fresh juice brings the sharpness.

steps.t: Wash the lemons and peel strips of zest from 2 with a peeler, avoiding the white pith.
Warm 200 ml water with the sugar and zest in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn off the heat and let the zest steep for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Meanwhile, juice all the lemons and strain: you need about 160 ml.
In a jug, combine the strained syrup, lemon juice and cold water; stir.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve over ice with a few mint leaves.

tips.t: Top with sparkling water just before serving for a fizzy lemonade.
It keeps for 3 days in a sealed bottle in the fridge.
A sprig of rosemary or thyme in the syrup gives it a garden scent.

title: Peach iced tea
intro: Made with real cooked peaches and briefly brewed black tea, never bitter.

steps.t: Chop the peaches with skin on, stone them and put them in a pan with the sugar and 200 ml water.
Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes, mashing with a fork, until the peaches fall apart.
steps.label: Peaches

steps.t: Meanwhile, heat 500 ml water to 95 °C, just short of boiling, turn off the heat and add the tea bags.
Steep for 4 minutes, then lift out the bags without squeezing them.
steps.label: Tea

steps.t: Strain the peaches, pressing hard with a spoon, and add the syrup to the tea.
Add 300 ml cold water and the lemon juice, then chill for 2 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve over ice with a few slices of fresh peach.

tips.t: Don't squeeze the tea bags: the tannins make the tea bitter and cloudy.
Green tea brewed at 80 °C with white peaches makes a gentler version.

title: Watermelon agua fresca
intro: Watermelon blended with lime and water: summer in a Mexican market.

steps.t: Cube the watermelon and remove as many black seeds as you can.
Blend the watermelon, water, lime juice and sugar for 30 seconds.
Strain through a sieve to remove the pulp and pour into a jug.
Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Stir, since it separates, and serve over ice with mint leaves.

tips.t: Same method works with melon, pineapple or cucumber: just swap the fruit.
Wet the glass rim with lime and dip it in salt and chilli powder.

title: Homemade ginger soda
intro: Fresh ginger syrup and sparkling water, with the bite of a ginger beer.

steps.t: Wash the ginger and grate it, skin and all.
Put the ginger, sugar and water in a pan, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Turn off the heat and steep for 20 minutes; the longer it sits, the hotter it gets.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Strain, pressing the ginger with a spoon, and chill the syrup for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: In each glass put ice, 50 ml syrup, the juice of half a lime and 200 ml sparkling water.
Stir gently just once and serve right away, while it's fizzy.

tips.t: The syrup keeps for 2 weeks in a sealed jar in the fridge.
Use this soda instead of ginger beer in a Moscow Mule.
A dried chilli or 2 cloves in the syrup give it more bite.

title: Ayran (salted yogurt drink)
intro: Yogurt, cold water and salt whisked until foamy: savoury and thirst-quenching.

steps.t: Put the yogurt and salt in a jug and whisk until smooth.
Add the cold water a little at a time, whisking all the while.
Whisk hard for 1 minute, or blend for 20 seconds, until a layer of foam forms.
Pour into chilled glasses and finish with a pinch of dried mint.

tips.t: Serve with kebabs, köfte or anything spicy: it cools the palate.
Use sparkling water instead of still and it's close to Persian doogh.

title: Chicha morada, purple corn drink
intro: Peru's purple drink: purple corn simmered with pineapple, apple, cinnamon and cloves.

steps.t: Peel the pineapple and apple, keeping the peels, and dice 150 g of pineapple. Break the corn cobs into 2 or 3 pieces.
Put the corn, pineapple peel and core, apple peel, cinnamon, cloves and water in a pot; simmer, covered.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Strain the deep purple liquid, pressing the solids well, and stir in the sugar while it's hot.
Let it cool, then chill for at least 2 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, stir in the lime juice and the diced pineapple and apple, and pour over ice.

tips.t: Add the lime only at the end: cooked or left too long, it makes the chicha bitter.
Dried purple corn is sold in Latin shops; there's also a powder that's ready in 15 minutes.
Without the lime, it keeps 3 days in a sealed bottle in the fridge.

title: Suco de maracujá, passion fruit juice
intro: Passion fruit pulp blended with water and sugar: tart and thirst-quenching.

steps.t: Halve the passion fruits and scoop the pulp and seeds into the blender jug.
Add half the water and pulse for a few seconds, just to free the pulp from the seeds.
Strain through a sieve, pressing with a spoon, and discard the seeds.
Add the rest of the water and the sugar and stir until it dissolves.
Serve right away, ice-cold, in glasses full of ice.

tips.t: Blend only a few seconds: crushed seeds make the juice bitter and cloudy.
Blend a few mint leaves with the pulp, or swap half the water for milk for a shake.

title: Cà phê sữa đá, Vietnamese iced coffee
intro: Strong coffee poured over condensed milk, then over ice: sweet, bitter and ice-cold.

steps.t: Fill the base of a 3-cup moka pot with water up to the valve, add the coffee without tamping and heat over low heat.
steps.label: Moka pot

steps.t: Put 2 tbsp condensed milk in each glass.
Pour the hot coffee over the milk and stir until dissolved and creamy.
Fill the glasses with ice, stir again and serve with a straw.

tips.t: With a phin filter: 20 g coffee per cup, a splash of water to bloom, then 100 ml; it drips in 5 minutes.
Skip the ice and it's cà phê sữa nóng, the hot version for Hanoi's winter mornings.

title: Cha yen, Thai iced tea
intro: Strong spiced black tea with condensed milk, poured over ice and topped with milk.

ing.n: strong loose black tea (Assam or Ceylon)

steps.t: Bring the water to a boil with the star anise, turn off the heat, add the tea and steep 5 minutes: it should be very strong.
steps.label: Steep

steps.t: Strain, add the sugar, condensed milk and vanilla and stir until dissolved. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Fill 2 tall glasses with ice and pour in the tea to three-quarters full.
Top each glass with 2 tbsp milk, which drifts down through the tea in clouds. Stir at the table.

tips.t: Thai tea mix from Asian shops, already spiced, gives the classic bright orange colour.
Leave out the milk and add sugar and lime juice for cha manao, Thai iced lime tea.

title: Jallab, date and grape drink
intro: Date, grape and rose water syrup over ice, topped with pine nuts and raisins.

steps.t: Put the pine nuts and raisins in a bowl of cold water and soak for 30 minutes, until plump.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: In a jug stir the jallab syrup into the cold water; taste and adjust the sweetness.
Fill four tall glasses with crushed ice and pour in the jallab.
Drain the pine nuts and raisins, spoon them on top and serve with a long spoon.

tips.t: No jallab syrup? Mix 3 parts date syrup, 1 part grape molasses and a few drops of rose water.
Crushed ice is a must: in Lebanon jallab is drunk ice-cold, almost like a slush.

title: Agua de jamaica (hibiscus drink)
intro: A ruby-red hibiscus drink, tart and refreshing, served over ice.

steps.t: Quickly rinse the hibiscus flowers in a sieve.
Bring 500 ml water to a boil, add the flowers and simmer.
steps.label: Hibiscus

steps.t: Turn off the heat, stir in the sugar and let it steep.
steps.label: Steeping

steps.t: Strain into a jug, pressing the flowers, add the cold water and lime juice; taste and adjust the sugar.
Chill in the fridge and serve in glasses full of ice.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Add a cinnamon stick and 2 cloves while steeping for a wintry version.
The used flowers, sautéed with onion and garlic, make a meatless taco filling.

title: Horchata de chufa, tiger nut milk
intro: Valencia's summer drink: sweet, nutty tiger nut milk served ice-cold.

steps.t: The day before, rinse the tiger nuts well, rubbing them between your hands to remove any soil; discard any that float.
Cover with plenty of cold water and soak in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours, changing the water once, until plump.
Drain, rinse and blend with the cold water for 2 to 3 minutes until very fine.
Let the mixture rest in the fridge so it releases all its flavour.
steps.label: Steep

steps.t: Strain through a nut milk bag or clean cloth, squeezing hard to get out all the liquid.
Dissolve the sugar in the horchata and chill; serve ice-cold, shaking it first as it separates.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Many Valencian homes add a piece of cinnamon stick and a strip of lemon peel while it steeps.
Freeze half and blend it with the rest for horchata granizada, as served in horchaterías.
Drink within 2 days as it ferments quickly; dry the leftover pulp in the oven and bake it into cookies.
